_doc: The rules of the Prairie Avenue DISTRICT DRAFT (owner, 2026-10-08; T-2159, split to T-2329 and T-2330). tools/draft_prairie_1904.py reads this file, the traced Sanborn footprints (data/traces/prairie_1904_footprints_s<sheet>.json), the sheet census and the T-1837 frontage register, and writes one prairie_draft structure record per building. A later block is drafted by ADDING rows here (a sheet under `blocks`, its frontages under `frontages`), never by editing the tool. Every number below is a RECONSTRUCTION bounded by the study's starting ranges (RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md) and recorded as one liberty per block in docs/LIBERTIES.md.

fit._doc: How a traced part becomes rectangles: the part is scan-filled on a grid in its lot's own frame, and the largest rectangle inside the fill is taken, then the largest in what is left, until the rectangles cover `coverage` of the fill or `max_rects` are taken. A rectangle smaller than `min_rect_m2` or thinner than `min_side_m` is not taken; one lying `swallowed` or more inside an earlier rectangle of the building is dropped.

heights._doc: Masonry houses: principal storey 3.9 m and upper storeys 3.5, 3.3 and 3.1 m floor to floor (RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md: principal 3.2-4.2, upper 2.9-3.7), over a basement whose principal floor stands 1.4 m above grade (the K01 contract's 0.8-1.8). Service buildings: a 3.4 m carriage storey and a 2.8 m loft. A half storey is the roof's: a mansard's 3.0 m lower face, or dormers in a hip.

28.where: Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28)

skip.s28-1800-front: 1800 Prairie is the Glessner house, the canonical benchmark (data/structures/glessner_house.json); the draft is judged beside it and never touches it.
skip.s28-1808-front: 1808 Prairie already stands as the K01 frontage assembly (data/structures/keith_house_1808_prairie.json), well past a draft; T-1882 and T-1883 refine that record, not this pass.
skip.s28-1812-rear: 1812's coach house is being built from the K12 kit as wheeler_house_1812_prairie_coach_house (T-2321, PR #666); the draft does not stand a second building in its place.

frontage-28-038.why: The register's 'high shaped gable and attic grid window' on a 3B rowhouse: the shaped gable is the house's silhouette, so it is the one feature drawn; the oriel and balcony are T-1884's.

frontage-28-039.why: Second Empire: the register's mansard with dormers over the mapped rounded front bays, which the fitted plan carries as a projecting bay.

frontage-28-040.why: 2½B on the map: two full storeys and a half in the roof, read as dormers in a hip behind the stone front.

frontage-28-041.why: A stone-front house with no named form: the stone-front family's flat roof behind a cornice.

frontage-28-042.why: The register's 'recorded 1886 mansard storey': 3S.B. read as three storeys and the mansard over them.

frontage-28-043.why: Second Empire: slate mansard and dormers over the mapped corner bay.

frontage-28-044.why: Italianate stone front with the register's 'deep bracketed cornice'; 1908 is attached and the census rules the two one building, so one record carries both fronts.

frontage-28-046.why: Chateauesque: the register's 'conical corner turret' and 'steep slate roof'; 2½B read as dormers in the steep hip.

frontage-28-047.why: 2½S.B. with a 'bay4B': a bay carried a storey above the house, drawn as a corner tower; its corner is not read off the sheet and is reconstructed.

frontage-28-048.skip: The census rules 1936 an alias of 1918 with no footprint of its own (no dwelling drawn on the lot).
